findings.description: Every debt gap now blocks the refresh, including capabilities that were never available and are missing from the stored baseline. Projects without vulture, pytest-cov or vitest coverage now fail every `pup audit` (and `--sweep`) for good with "Baseline kept".
findings.body:
**A metric that was never measured now blocks every audit, not just one whose measurement failed.**

Whenever a stored baseline exists, `auditProject` turns every entry of `report.gaps` into an `unmeasured` line. It never checks whether the previous baseline actually held a figure for that metric:

```ts
const unmeasured = previous
  ? report.gaps.map(
      (gap) =>
        `${sanitizeReason(gap.adapterId)}: ${gap.capability} not measured — ${sanitizeReason(gap.reason)}`,
    )
  : [];
if (unmeasured.length === 0) persistBaseline(db, report.projectId, report.baseline);
```

The built-in adapters return `{ unavailable }` for permanent setup reasons as well as for failed runs. `measureDebt` (`src/core/debt.service.ts`) only skips a capability whose method is missing, so each of these becomes a gap on every run:

- `typescript.adapter.ts` L307-308: `no vitest + @vitest/coverage-* in package.json`. This hits every Jest-based or test-less TS repo.
- `python.adapter.ts` L293-294: `no vulture declared …`
- `python.adapter.ts` L346-347: `no pytest-cov declared …`

For these projects, `pup init` stores a baseline with no `coverageRatio` or `deadExports`. Every later `pup audit` then hits the same gap, prints "Baseline kept … Fix the measurement" and exits 1. The CLI check at `src/cli/index.ts` L1926-1931 runs before the `opts.sweep` branch, so `pup audit --sweep` is blocked the same way. Before this PR these audits refreshed normally. The refusal is protecting a figure the stored baseline never had.

The motivating incident and the new tests both cover a metric that measured at init and then broke. A suggested fix is to block only when the gap would drop a figure the previous baseline holds:

- a coverage gap when `previous.debt?.coverageRatio !== undefined`
- a dead-code gap when `previous.debt?.deadExports !== undefined`

In a multi-adapter repo, dead code is still an edge case: `deadExports` is stored flat, not per adapter.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/f91f702352da5ccd1c0d2ba4d86828c56289be2a/src/core/audit.service.ts#L138-L144

findings.description: When the audit refuses because a metric went unmeasured, it returns before printing the stage and debt transitions it computed, so the operator sees no drift report.

The `auditProject` JSDoc still says it refreshes the baseline unconditionally. It also claims 'nothing is written to be undone', but `measureBaseline` still writes the project row and origin URL (`ensureProject`/`recordOriginUrl`) before a kept-baseline refusal; only the baseline and its history row are held back.

The call-site comment 'A failed measurement is not a figure…' repeats the `auditProject`/`AuditOutcome.unmeasured` JSDoc and the 'Baseline kept' message (AGENTS.md §Comments: a call-site copy of the seam's WHY is a duplicate).
The test comment repeats the test title and the `src/cli/index.ts` comment; delete it or cut it to one line.
The test comment narrates the triggering incident (half-applied fast-forward). That belongs in the commit/PR text, since the test title already states the behaviour.
The `persistBaseline` JSDoc mostly restates the function name; the real WHY (history seeding) is already in the inline comment inside the function.

Decision 38 in docs/09-decisions.md names `initProject` as the one choke point that appends baseline history. That append now lives in `persistBaseline`, called directly by `auditProject`, and the new rule (an unmeasured metric keeps the baseline and appends no row) is not recorded.

Core formats the user-facing 'not measured' lines while the CLI composes the rest of the same refusal. Returning structured `DebtGap[]` and formatting in the CLI would keep one refusal's presentation in one layer.
`initProject` destructures four fields from `measureBaseline` and rebuilds the object only to drop `gaps`; `const { gaps: _gaps, ...report } = measureBaseline(...)` says the same thing more directly.
